Real biology, engineered with precision.

Starting point

A well-defined problem in animal health, still unresolved after decades

Animal production faces parasites and pathogens for which the available solutions are increasingly ineffective, costly, or prone to resistance over time. Sea lice (Lepeophtheirus salmonis, Caligus rogercresseyi) affecting salmon aquaculture are a clear example of this type of challenge.

This is Knotide Bio's first application case: demonstrating, on a real and measurable problem, how a well-engineered biomolecule can replace approaches worn down by resistance.

An industry under constant pressure Sea lice control has been estimated at around one billion US dollars per year in direct treatment costs, with indirect losses from mortality and reduced production estimated at several times that figure, according to industry estimates cited in EU-funded research projects.

Platform

From biomolecule to product, with scientific rigour at every stage

Knotide Bio explores families of bioactive peptides and proteins as the starting point for designing biotechnological solutions directed at specific targets in animal health.

  1. 01

    Discovery

    Bioprospecting and selection of biomolecules with potential activity against identified targets.

  2. 02

    Characterisation

    Study of the structure and function of selected molecules, and their mechanism of action.

  3. 03

    Validation

    Laboratory assays and analyses confirming activity, selectivity and safety.

  4. 04

    Application

    Formulation and integration of validated biomolecules into solutions for animal health, nutrition and welfare.

AI-guided molecular design

Knotide Bio develops small, highly stable biological molecules, bioactive peptides designed with the support of AI-based tools to selectively block critical infection and adhesion steps, without relying on direct toxicity.

This design approach favours precision over broad-spectrum action: molecules are shaped to fit a specific interaction surface, reducing off-target effects and the selective pressure that drives resistance.

Illustrative structural rendering, conceptual and not experimental data.

Engineering biology at the molecular level.

Applications

Three complementary pillars in animal production

Animal health

Biomolecules directed at parasites and pathogens relevant to animal production, offering an alternative to resistance-prone solutions.

Animal nutrition

Bioactive peptides and proteins applied in nutritional solutions that support animal performance and gut health.

Animal welfare

Solutions that reduce the need for intensive handling and treatment, with direct benefit for animal welfare.

Poultry
Swine

Illustrative example

In our lead application, a Knotide Bio peptide is designed to interrupt a critical step an external parasite needs to attach to and colonise its host. The molecule targets a defined biological interaction rather than relying on broad toxicity, an approach we are extending to other pathogens, targets and species within the platform.

Knotide Bio's first application case is sea lice in salmon aquaculture, a problem with significant economic impact and no dominant biotechnological solution, chosen as the entry point to validate the platform ahead of other species and parasites.

Services

Beyond in-house development, in service of third parties

Knotide Bio's activity is not limited to developing its own platform. The company also provides specialised services to other biotechnology and life sciences organisations.

  • Research & development

    Research, development and commercialisation of biotechnology-based biomolecules, namely bioactive peptides and proteins.

  • Production

    Production of biomolecules, either directly or through subcontracting to third parties, depending on project stage and scale.

  • Scientific & technical consultancy

    Scientific, technical and technological consultancy in biotechnology and life sciences for third-party organisations.

  • Laboratory testing & validation

    Technical and laboratory assays, analyses and validations for the characterisation, development and quality control of biomolecules and biotechnology products.

Knotide Bio brings together a multidisciplinary founding team with complementary expertise spanning microbiology, molecular biotechnology, biochemical engineering, biomolecule discovery and industrial innovation.

The team combines three backgrounds in microbiology, including postgraduate training in molecular microbiology, with PhD-level expertise in biochemical engineering and biotechnology and postgraduate training in business management. Together, the team brings more than four decades of combined experience across R&D, industrial innovation, biomolecule engineering, project leadership and national and European research and innovation funding, including FCT, Horizon Europe and COMPETE2020/2030 programmes.

Our expertise covers the discovery, engineering and development of bioactive molecules, supported by strong capabilities in molecular engineering, physicochemical and structural characterisation, formulation, functional evaluation and validation. The team has experience across the full R&D pathway, from scientific concept and early discovery through development and validation to industrial implementation.

This scientific expertise is complemented by extensive experience in leading multidisciplinary R&D programmes and translating research into industrial innovation. Collectively, the team has managed R&D programmes involving more than €40 million in funding and has led projects supported by major national and European funding instruments.

The founding team also maintains strong links with academic and research institutions, providing access to scientific expertise, technology platforms and collaborative opportunities. These connections include the University of Porto and its associated research and innovation ecosystem, as well as collaborations with international academic and industrial organisations.

At Knotide Bio, these complementary capabilities converge around a common objective: to engineer and develop bioactive molecules with the potential to generate next-generation solutions for disease prevention and treatment.
